content.text:
Reading the structure region by region:

- **Quinoline core:** N1 is at the bottom, C2 is the CH, C3 carries the 3,5-difluorophenyl group, and C4 carries the piperidine nitrogen. C4a and C8a are the fusion carbons, and C6 carries the aryl substituent.
- **Piperidine:** the ring nitrogen is attached to C4 of the quinoline, and the carbon opposite the nitrogen bears NH2 (4-aminopiperidin-1-yl).
- **Difluorophenyl:** attached at C3 of the quinoline, with fluorines meta to the attachment point (3,5-difluoro).
- **Right-hand benzene ring:** attached to C6 of the quinoline. Its ortho carbon carries OH, and the next carbon carries C≡N. The ring is therefore 3-(quinolin-6-yl)-2-hydroxybenzonitrile.

Quinoline SMILES: c1nc2ccc(cc2c(N3CCC(N)CC3)c1-c1cc(F)cc(F)c1)-c1cccc(C#N)c1O

Checking the quinoline ring: c1 (C2), n (N1), c2 (C8a), c (C8), c (C7), c( (C6) with the substituent after the branch, c (C5), c2 (C4a), then c(N-piperidine) (C4), then c1 (C3) closing the ring back to C2. The ring closure is correct, and the difluorophenyl is on C3. The C6 branch is opened with "(" after C6, containing "cc2c(...)c1-Ar", and the aryl group follows as -c1cccc(C#N)c1O. In that branch the ring-1 label is reused after being closed at C3, which is valid because the first label-1 closure happens at "c1-c1cc(F)..." — to avoid ambiguity I rewrite it with distinct ring numbers.

Rewritten SMILES: N#Cc1cccc(c1O)-c1ccc2ncc(-c3cc(F)cc(F)c3)c(N3CCC(N)CC3)c2c1

Checking this version: c1ccc2ncc(...)c(...)c2c1 starts at C6 (the attachment atom), then C7, C8, C8a (c2), N, C2, C3 (with the difluorophenyl), C4 (with the piperidine), C4a (c2 closing the fusion ring), and C5 (c1 closing back to C6). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: N#Cc1cccc(c1O)-c1ccc2ncc(-c3cc(F)cc(F)c3)c(N3CCC(N)CC3)c2c1
